outcome: maternal systemic inflammation (plasma C-reactive protein, white blood cell count)
fetal growth (birth weight for gestational age z score)
cohort: The study included 1808 mother-child pairs from Project Viva.
finding: Higher maternal prenatal dietary inflammatory index (DII) scores were associated with higher second-trimester plasma C-reactive protein, lower birth weight for gestational age z-score in infants born to obese mothers, and lower odds of breastfeeding for at least 1 month.
